top_signals.title: Oaktree’s Playbook for Rising Credit Stress
top_signals.summary: As higher rates bite and SEC scrutiny rises, Danielle Poli, a Managing Director and Co-Portfolio Manager at Oaktree, joins Bloomberg Open Interest to break down where credit risk is really building, and where the best opportunities are. From complex data-center deals to looming refinancings and distressed software names, she explains how smart credit investors are positioning. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Inside the Toys "R" Us Comeback
top_signals.summary: WHP Global is bringing Toys "R" Us back to life with over 120 new US stores despite falling consumer confidence. Yehuda Shmidman, the founder, chairman and CEO of the brand licensing company WHP Global, joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why toy demand is surging, the rise of the “kidult” shopper, and how an asset‑light licensing model is powering billions in sales and potential IPO plans. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Public companies produce most U.S. crude oil and natural gas
top_signals.summary: Publicly traded companies represent a tiny share of the total number of companies producing crude oil and natural gas in the United States, but they make up a large share of U.S. production. In 2025, publicly traded companies accounted for just 2% of about 12,000 oil and natural gas producers but produced 68% of the crude oil and natural gas in the Lower 48 states.
